Shaco.escape: The moment after Shaco uses Q Deceive is your chance to close the gap. When Shaco appears, place Kindred W Wolf's Frenzy, follow with Kindred Q Dance of Arrows, and attack with your allies. Don't force a chase into areas without vision where Shaco W Jack In The Box may be placed.
Shaco.teamfight: Don't engage first. After an ally starts the fight, place Kindred W Wolf's Frenzy behind your team and attack while repositioning with Kindred Q Dance of Arrows. If Shaco uses Q Deceive to engage and appears, focus your damage with your allies immediately. If an allied carry is caught, you can save them with Kindred R Lamb's Respite, but enemies will survive too, so be ready to finish them as soon as the zone ends.
Shaco.watch: Shaco Q Deceive lets him stealth and get behind you, where his empowered basic attack is dangerous, so if you think Shaco is nearby, keep your back to a wall or face your allies. Shaco W Jack In The Box can fear you from brush without vision or around objectives, so check those areas first with a Control Ward or Oracle Lens. When low on health, watch out for the finishing damage from Shaco E Two-Shiv Poison and don't travel through areas without vision.
Shaco.fight: The moment after Shaco Q Deceive ends is a chance to focus your damage with allies. Place Kindred W Wolf's Frenzy where you plan to fight, then keep attacking the same target while repositioning with Kindred Q Dance of Arrows inside it. If Shaco uses R Hallucinate, identify the real one by watching health bar reactions so you don't waste damage on the clone.
Shaco.laning: Early on, keep vision at your jungle entrances to guard against Shaco's ganks and invades. Plan your camp route around the direction of Kindred P Mark of the Kindred, but only go for marks deep in the enemy jungle without vision when your team has lane priority. If a gank looks uncertain, focus on farming and securing marks instead of forcing it.
Shaco.build: Build magic resistance first against damage from Shaco W Jack In The Box, E Two-Shiv Poison, and R Hallucinate. Get health so you don't easily enter the health range where Shaco E Two-Shiv Poison damage becomes high, and consider movement speed to escape areas where boxes are placed.
Shaco.combo: Place Kindred W Wolf's Frenzy first, then slow Shaco with Kindred E Mounting Dread. If Shaco looks ready to escape with Q Deceive, use Kindred E Mounting Dread first to apply the slow.
Shaco.phase: Early on, Kindred is fragile and has low movement speed, while Shaco looks for an advantage through ganks and invades, so prioritize farming and marks without giving up kills. Kindred starts to become a duelist in mid game as marks and attack speed items build up. If you buy time into the late game, Shaco's ability to fight alone falls off, and Kindred can use the range gained from marks.

Jax.phase: Later, increased range from marks makes it easier to fight the melee champion Jax, so securing early marks is important.
Jax.laning: Early on, do not fight Jax for long; prioritize marks and farming. Attempt a mark in enemy territory without vision only when your team has lane priority, and look for ganks when an ally has reliable crowd control or the enemy has pushed too far.
Jax.teamfight: Do not engage first. Wait for an ally to start the fight, then place Kindred W Wolf's Frenzy behind your team and position with Kindred Q Dance of Arrows inside its area. If Jax engages with Jax Q Leap Strike and activates Jax E Counter Strike, do not group up, stop basic attacking, and avoid the stun area. You can save a carry who is caught with Kindred R Lamb's Respite, but account for Jax surviving inside the zone and finish him as it ends.
Jax.build: Prioritize attack speed items alongside mark growth. Jax Q Leap Strike deals physical damage, while Jax W Empower and Jax E Counter Strike deal magic damage, so do not focus your resistance build on only one type.
Jax.combo: Place Kindred W Wolf's Frenzy first and apply Kindred E Mounting Dread to Jax. After Jax E Counter Strike ends, use Kindred Q Dance of Arrows and basic attacks to trigger Wolf's pounce, without switching targets.
Jax.escape: The moment after Jax uses Jax Q Leap Strike is a window to engage, especially if Jax E Counter Strike is also down. Manage distance with Kindred Q Dance of Arrows and fight inside Kindred W Wolf's Frenzy.
Jax.fight: Look for a damage-trading opportunity after Jax E Counter Strike is down. Place Kindred W Wolf's Frenzy first and reposition with Kindred Q Dance of Arrows inside its area, then deal damage with basic attacks while Jax has no Counter Strike.
Jax.watch: When Jax E Counter Strike is active, your basic attacks are negated, and he can reactivate it to stun in an area, so stop basic attacking and use Kindred Q Dance of Arrows to get outside its range. Jax Q Leap Strike is an engage tool, so watch for it and keep your distance.

Brand.teamfight: Don’t engage first. After an ally starts the fight, cast Kindred W Wolf’s Frenzy behind your team and attack while repositioning with Kindred Q Dance of Arrows inside the zone. Stay away from burning allies so Brand E Conflagration and Brand R Pyroclasm don’t spread. Kindred R Lamb’s Respite also saves enemies, so use it carefully when you need to save a key damage dealer, then finish the enemy as the zone ends.
Brand.laning: Early on, prioritize farming and securing Kindred P Mark of the Kindred over risky engages, and plan your camp route around the mark. Only contest a deep mark in the enemy jungle without vision when your allies have lane priority. Avoid standing near minions Brand has set ablaze, and look for ganks when an ally has reliable crowd control or Brand has pushed the lane too far.
Brand.build: Get attack speed items to improve your midgame dueling. If you build resistances against Brand’s damage, choose magic resistance. Armor won’t help against Brand’s magic damage, and stacking only health also increases the damage from Brand P Blaze, which scales with maximum health.
Brand.combo: When Brand W Pillar of Flame is down, cast Kindred W Wolf’s Frenzy first, then approach and position with Kindred Q Dance of Arrows inside the zone. Apply Kindred E Mounting Dread to Brand, use Q to gain attack speed, then keep basic attacking to trigger Wolf’s pounce. Switching targets during this sequence means you have to build up E’s stacks again.
Brand.escape: Brand has no mobility, so the moment after he casts Brand W Pillar of Flame is your chance to close the distance. If you’re ablaze, Brand Q Sear can stun you, so dodge it first, then engage with Kindred Q Dance of Arrows and Kindred W Wolf’s Frenzy.
Brand.fight: When Brand W Pillar of Flame is down, cast Kindred W Wolf’s Frenzy and use Kindred Q Dance of Arrows to close the distance. If you’re ablaze, dodge the stun from Brand Q Sear first, then keep attacking the same target. Kindred’s physical damage is effective against Brand’s low armor.
Brand.phase: Early on, Kindred is fragile and slow, so prioritize marks and farming over risky fights with Brand. You can duel from midgame onward once you have marks and attack speed items. In late game, use the range gained from your marks, but if you missed marks, that growth will be harder to achieve.
Brand.watch: After Brand P Blaze is applied, Brand Q Sear stuns you, so use Kindred Q Dance of Arrows to dodge the projectile while ablaze. Dodging Brand W Pillar of Flame also makes it easier to break his combo before it builds more Blaze stacks. In teamfights, spread out from allies to prevent Brand E Conflagration from spreading and Brand R Pyroclasm from bouncing.

Ekko.laning: Early on, prioritize farming and securing marks over risky ganks. Only contest a deep mark in Ekko’s jungle without vision when your allies have lane priority. Look for ganks when an ally has reliable crowd control or the opponent has pushed the lane too far.
Ekko.build: Prioritize attack speed items to keep pace with your mark growth. If the healing from Ekko R Chronobreak is a problem, get Mortal Reminder for Grievous Wounds, and build magic resistance against Ekko’s magic damage.
Ekko.combo: Cast Kindred W Wolf’s Frenzy first where you plan to fight. Apply Kindred E Mounting Dread to Ekko, weave in Kindred Q Dance of Arrows to gain attack speed, then keep basic attacking without switching targets. If Ekko might escape with his mobility, use E early for its slow.
Ekko.escape: Dodge the stun from Ekko W Parallel Convergence and engage when Ekko R Chronobreak is down. If only Ekko E Phase Dive is down, he can still escape with Ekko R Chronobreak, so don’t overcommit. Once both abilities are down, close the distance with Kindred Q Dance of Arrows and Kindred W Wolf’s Frenzy.
Ekko.fight: Look to fight after Ekko R Chronobreak is down. Dodge the signal for Ekko W Parallel Convergence, then keep attacking the same target while repositioning with Kindred Q Dance of Arrows inside Kindred W Wolf’s Frenzy. If Ekko might escape with Ekko E Phase Dive, apply Kindred E Mounting Dread early.
Ekko.phase: Early on, Kindred is fragile and slow, so prioritize marks and farming over risky fights with Ekko. You can look for duels in midgame once you have marks and attack speed items. In late game, use the range gained from your marks, but don’t engage first expecting that growth if you missed marks.
Ekko.teamfight: After an ally starts the fight, cast Kindred W Wolf’s Frenzy behind your team and attack while repositioning with Kindred Q Dance of Arrows inside the zone. If you see the signal for Ekko W Parallel Convergence, dodge its area, and look for an opening just after Ekko engages with Ekko E Phase Dive, while his mobility is down. If a key allied damage dealer is caught, save them with Kindred R Lamb’s Respite, but keep in mind Ekko can survive inside the zone and heal when it ends; finish him immediately afterward.
Ekko.watch: When you see the signal for Ekko W Parallel Convergence, stay out of its area to avoid the stun and shield. Use Kindred Q Dance of Arrows to dodge the return path of Ekko Q Timewinder. If you see Ekko’s afterimage, Ekko R Chronobreak is ready, so do not let a low health bar tempt you into a reckless chase.

Gragas.teamfight: Do not engage first while Gragas E Body Slam is available. Wait for an ally to start the fight, then place Kindred W Wolf's Frenzy behind your team. Attack while repositioning with Kindred Q Dance of Arrows inside its area, and if Gragas E Body Slam hits you, immediately move outside Gragas Q Barrel Roll's radius. Use Kindred R Lamb's Respite to save an allied carry caught by an engage, then finish enemies as the zone ends.
Gragas.laning: Early on, plan your camp route toward marks and keep farming instead of forcing ganks. Gragas may wait near a mark, so attempt a deep mark in enemy territory without vision only when your team has lane priority. Look for ganks when an ally has reliable crowd control or the enemy has pushed too far.
Gragas.build: To counter the healing from Gragas P Happy Hour, get healing reduction and armor penetration with Mortal Reminder. Build magic resistance against Gragas's main damage, and avoid stacking health alone because Gragas W Drunken Rage deals damage based on your maximum health.
Gragas.combo: Place Kindred W Wolf's Frenzy first, then apply Kindred E Mounting Dread inside its area and keep attacking the same target with Kindred Q Dance of Arrows and basic attacks. If Gragas looks ready to escape with Gragas E Body Slam, apply Kindred E Mounting Dread's slow first, then focus your finishing damage after Gragas W Drunken Rage's damage reduction ends.
Gragas.escape: The moment after Gragas uses Gragas E Body Slam is your chance to close the gap. Place Kindred W Wolf's Frenzy and approach with Kindred Q Dance of Arrows, but stay outside Gragas Q Barrel Roll's radius.
Gragas.fight: Fight by placing Kindred W Wolf's Frenzy and using Kindred Q Dance of Arrows to manage distance as soon as Gragas E Body Slam is down. Save your burst while Gragas drinks with Gragas W Drunken Rage, then focus him after its damage reduction ends. Gragas can use E Body Slam again while fleeing, so chase only when you can finish him reliably.
Gragas.phase: Early on, prioritize P Mark of the Kindred and farming while watching for Gragas's burst and ability to disrupt your formation. Kindred can duel from mid game, once marks and attack speed items have accumulated. In late game, use Kindred's range and sustained damage to fight while keeping your distance.
Gragas.watch: When you see Gragas Q Barrel Roll, use Kindred Q Dance of Arrows to get outside its radius. If Gragas E Body Slam hits you near the barrel, you can be hit by both abilities, so keep your distance while Gragas E Body Slam is available. Position yourself so Gragas R Explosive Cask does not knock you toward the enemy team.

Ivern.teamfight: Do not engage first. Wait for an ally to start the fight, then place Kindred W Wolf's Frenzy behind your team and attack while repositioning with Kindred Q Dance of Arrows inside its area. Kindred R Lamb's Respite also saves enemies, so use it when an allied carry is caught and damage opponents inside the zone so you can finish them as it ends.
Ivern.watch: If Ivern Q Rootcaller roots you, Ivern's allies can dash in, so avoid the angle before he casts by keeping minions or terrain between you. Do not engage a target affected by Ivern E Triggerseed until the shield bursts. If Ivern R Daisy! starts hitting you, reposition to avoid being knocked up by her repeated attacks.
Ivern.laning: Early on, plan your camp route toward marks, and attempt a deep mark in Ivern's territory without vision only when your team has lane priority. If you get vision on a camp Ivern has seeded, you can read his route when he comes to harvest it. Do not casually walk past newly created Ivern W Brushmaker brush.
Ivern.combo: After Ivern Q Rootcaller is down and Ivern E Triggerseed's shield has burst, place Kindred W Wolf's Frenzy first. Apply Kindred E Mounting Dread to one target, use Kindred Q Dance of Arrows to increase your attack speed, then keep basic attacking. Do not switch targets while Kindred E Mounting Dread is applied.
Ivern.escape: The moment after Ivern uses Ivern Q Rootcaller is your window to engage. Close the gap with Kindred Q Dance of Arrows and Kindred W Wolf's Frenzy, but wait until Ivern E Triggerseed's shield bursts before engaging its target.
Ivern.fight: Close the gap as soon as Ivern Q Rootcaller is down. Place Kindred W Wolf's Frenzy first, then attack while repositioning with Kindred Q Dance of Arrows inside its area. Delay engaging a target already affected by Ivern E Triggerseed until the shield bursts.
Ivern.phase: Early on, Kindred is fragile, so prioritize marks and farming over forcing fights. In mid game, Kindred can duel once P Mark of the Kindred and attack speed items have accumulated, and further range growth depends on collecting marks on time.
Ivern.build: The source does not specify a starting item. If you build resistance against Ivern's damaging abilities, choose magic resistance over armor. However, the risk of allies joining in following Ivern Q Rootcaller's root and Ivern R Daisy!'s knock-up is high, so you often need to prioritize tenacity.

Karthus.laning: Early on, plan your camp route toward the mark. Only go for marks deep in the enemy jungle without vision when your team has lane priority. If a gank opportunity is uncertain, focus on farming and collecting marks instead of forcing it.
Karthus.teamfight: Don’t engage first. After an ally starts the fight, place Kindred W Wolf’s Frenzy behind your team and attack while repositioning inside it with Kindred Q Dance of Arrows. Clear the frontline before Karthus gets within Karthus E Defile range, and don’t stay by Karthus’s corpse if you kill him. If Karthus R Requiem is about to kill an ally, Kindred R Lamb’s Respite can keep them alive, but remember that enemies inside also survive and heal when it ends.
Karthus.build: The available information isn’t enough to determine a specific first item. Against Karthus’s damage, prioritize magic resistance over armor. However, avoiding Karthus W Wall of Pain and quickly leaving Karthus E Defile’s area matter more.
Karthus.combo: Place Kindred W Wolf’s Frenzy where Karthus will stand, then fight inside the zone. Apply Kindred E Mounting Dread, close in with Kindred Q Dance of Arrows to build attack speed, and keep basic attacking the same target to trigger Wolf’s pounce. Dodge the marked areas of Karthus Q Lay Waste with Kindred Q Dance of Arrows while repositioning inside the zone.
Karthus.escape: Karthus has no mobility or immobilizing effects, so you can approach after avoiding Karthus W Wall of Pain. Don’t enter across the wall; use Kindred Q Dance of Arrows to close the gap. If you end up staying in Karthus E Defile’s area for too long, use Kindred Q Dance of Arrows to get out.
Karthus.fight: Karthus has no way to create distance on his own, so look for a chance to approach while avoiding Karthus W Wall of Pain. Place Kindred W Wolf’s Frenzy first, then use Kindred Q Dance of Arrows to reposition inside it while continuing to attack the same target. Don’t stay in Karthus E Defile for long, and move away from his corpse after killing him.
Karthus.phase: By midgame, marks and attack speed items let Kindred duel effectively, but Karthus can catch up quickly through farming. The available information isn’t enough to determine who has the advantage late game, so make use of the increased range from marks and keep enough health to withstand Karthus R Requiem.
Karthus.watch: Passing through Karthus W Wall of Pain slows you and lowers your magic resistance, making the follow-up Karthus Q Lay Waste and R Requiem more dangerous. Go around the wall, and use Kindred Q Dance of Arrows to reposition out of Karthus Q Lay Waste’s marked blast areas. Karthus’s abilities can still go off right after he dies, so move away from his corpse immediately.

LeeSin.laning: Early on, plan your camp route toward marks, but only go for marks deep in Lee Sin’s jungle without vision when your team has lane priority. Look for ganks when an ally has reliable crowd control or the enemy has pushed their lane too far. Otherwise, focus on farming and securing vision.
LeeSin.watch: If your health is low, use Kindred Q Dance of Arrows to create distance and move toward your allies. Keep away from walls without vision, since Lee Sin W Safeguard / Iron Will can carry him over one.
LeeSin.combo: Place Kindred W Wolf’s Frenzy where the enemy will fight, then mark the same target with Kindred E Mounting Dread. Follow with Kindred Q Dance of Arrows to build attack speed, then keep basic attacking without switching targets to trigger Wolf’s pounce.
LeeSin.build: Build armor first against Lee Sin’s main damage from Q Sonic Wave / Resonating Strike and R Dragon’s Rage. Armor won’t block Lee Sin E Tempest / Cripple’s damage. If Lee Sin W Safeguard / Iron Will’s life steal makes the fight drag on, consider Grievous Wounds.
LeeSin.escape: Don’t engage just because Lee Sin Q Sonic Wave / Resonating Strike is down. If Lee Sin W Safeguard / Iron Will is down too, close the gap with Kindred Q Dance of Arrows and attack before Lee Sin Q Sonic Wave / Resonating Strike comes back up.
LeeSin.fight: Avoid direct duels with Lee Sin early. When fighting, place Kindred W Wolf’s Frenzy first, then reposition and attack inside it with Kindred Q Dance of Arrows. Focus your damage right after Lee Sin uses W Safeguard / Iron Will to engage.
LeeSin.phase: Lee Sin is strong in early duels, so back off if you meet him and prioritize marks and farming. Kindred can duel effectively from midgame once marks and attack speed items are in place. Late game, use the extra range from marks to fight while keeping your distance.
LeeSin.teamfight: After an ally starts the fight, place Kindred W Wolf’s Frenzy behind your team and attack while repositioning inside it with Kindred Q Dance of Arrows. Keep space from your allies to account for Lee Sin R Dragon’s Rage, and stand with a wall or your frontline behind you to make it harder for him to get around. If Lee Sin’s engage catches an allied carry, save them with Kindred R Lamb’s Respite and look to finish the fight as the zone ends.

MonkeyKing.laning: Early on, farm and plan your camp route toward marks instead of forcing a fight with Wukong. Only go for marks in the enemy jungle without vision when your team has lane priority. Look for ganks when an ally has reliable crowd control or the enemy has pushed their lane too far.
MonkeyKing.teamfight: Don’t engage first. After an ally starts the fight, place Kindred W Wolf’s Frenzy behind your team and attack while repositioning inside it with Kindred Q Dance of Arrows. Don’t group up while Wukong R Cyclone is available. If an allied carry is caught by Wukong’s engage, Kindred R Lamb’s Respite can save them. Kindred R Lamb’s Respite also saves Wukong, so lower his health beforehand to finish him as the zone ends.
MonkeyKing.build: Build armor first against Wukong’s main damage. If you need Grievous Wounds to counter healing from Wukong P Stone Skin, get Mortal Reminder for that along with armor penetration. Armor won’t block the magic damage from Wukong E Nimbus Strike.
MonkeyKing.combo: Place Kindred W Wolf’s Frenzy where the fight will happen. If Wukong can escape, apply Kindred E Mounting Dread first to slow him, then build attack speed with Kindred Q Dance of Arrows and keep basic attacking the same target. If Wukong W Warrior Trickster appears, don’t switch targets to chase the clone.
MonkeyKing.escape: After Wukong W Warrior Trickster is down, the window before it comes back up is your chance to engage. However, don’t go deep just because one mobility ability is down if Wukong E Nimbus Strike is still available. Right after Wukong R Cyclone is down too, look for a chance to force a fight or objective.
MonkeyKing.fight: Wukong P Stone Skin builds armor and healing the longer the fight goes on, so trade briefly and back off. If Wukong W Warrior Trickster appears, don’t waste attacks on the stationary clone; watch which way the real Wukong is heading. Before Wukong W Warrior Trickster comes back up, use Kindred Q Dance of Arrows to control the distance and pressure him again.
MonkeyKing.phase: Early on, Kindred is fragile and slow, so prioritize marks and farming over forced duels with Wukong. By midgame, once marks and attack speed items are in place, Kindred can duel effectively. Late game, if marks have increased your range, you can pressure the melee Wukong from outside his range, but you can’t count on that growth if you’ve missed marks.
MonkeyKing.watch: Wukong E Nimbus Strike is targeted, so it can’t be dodged while you’re in range. Wukong Q Crushing Blow reduces your armor if it hits, so keep your distance outside Wukong E Nimbus Strike range.

Nocturne.phase: Kindred is fragile and slow early, so avoid risky fights with the enemy jungler and focus on marks and farming. Duels become viable from midgame onward as you collect marks and attack speed items. In the late game, keep your distance if your marks have increased your range, but don’t step forward if you missed marks and fell behind in growth.
Nocturne.teamfight: Don’t engage first. After your team starts a fight, place Kindred W Wolf’s Frenzy behind your allies. When Nocturne R Paranoia is activated, stay close to your allies and attack while adjusting your position with Kindred Q Dance of Arrows from within the zone. If Nocturne dives onto your team’s main damage dealer, save them with Kindred R Lamb’s Respite, then finish him as the zone ends.
Nocturne.watch: When Nocturne R Paranoia darkens your screen, don’t stay isolated; immediately move toward your allies. If Nocturne E Unspeakable Horror connects, use Kindred Q Dance of Arrows to create distance and break the tether before the fear triggers. Be careful not to use Kindred E Mounting Dread immediately while Nocturne W Shroud of Darkness is available.
Nocturne.laning: Keep routing your camps toward the marked side, but only contest a mark deep in the enemy jungle without vision when your team has lane priority. Maintain vision at river and jungle entrances so you know where to retreat before Nocturne R Paranoia is activated. If you’re hit by Nocturne Q Duskbringer, don’t run straight away; angle toward an ally or turret.
Nocturne.build: Build armor first against the physical damage from Nocturne P Umbra Blades, Nocturne Q Duskbringer, and Nocturne R Paranoia. If the healing from Nocturne P Umbra Blades is a problem, get healing reduction and armor penetration with Mortal Reminder. Armor can’t block the magic damage from Nocturne E Unspeakable Horror.
Nocturne.combo: Place Kindred W Wolf’s Frenzy first, then mark one target with Kindred E Mounting Dread from within the zone. Follow with Kindred Q Dance of Arrows to gain attack speed and keep basic attacking the same target to trigger the wolf’s pounce. If Nocturne W Shroud of Darkness is active, break the spell shield with another ability first, then apply Kindred E Mounting Dread.
Nocturne.escape: If Nocturne E Unspeakable Horror is down, close the gap with Kindred W Wolf’s Frenzy and Kindred Q Dance of Arrows without worrying about the fear. Once Nocturne W Shroud of Darkness is also down, apply Kindred E Mounting Dread to set up its slow and finishing damage.
Nocturne.fight: Early on, prioritize marks and farming over risky jungle duels. While Nocturne R Paranoia is down, place Kindred W Wolf’s Frenzy first, then attack from within the zone while positioning with Kindred Q Dance of Arrows. Keep yourself in a position where you can use Kindred Q Dance of Arrows if Nocturne E Unspeakable Horror catches you.

Poppy.teamfight: Don’t step forward first while Poppy E Heroic Charge is available. After an ally starts the fight, place Kindred W Wolf’s Frenzy behind your team, watch Poppy W Steadfast Presence, and reposition inside the zone with Kindred Q Dance of Arrows. If Poppy’s engage puts an allied carry at risk of dying, save them with Kindred R Lamb’s Respite and look to finish the fight as the zone ends.
Poppy.laning: Avoid Poppy E Heroic Charge’s stun by not standing with a wall or narrow passage behind you. Only go for marks in the enemy jungle without vision when your team has lane priority. If the gank angle is uncertain, focus on farming and securing marks. If Poppy’s thrown shield lands, step on it first to prevent her from gaining a shield.
Poppy.build: Build armor first against the main damage from Poppy Q Hammer Shock, Poppy E Heroic Charge, and Poppy R Keeper’s Verdict. Poppy Q Hammer Shock deals damage based on maximum health, so avoid investing heavily in health alone. Don’t spend resources on magic resistance specifically for Poppy.
Poppy.combo: After Poppy W Steadfast Presence ends, place Kindred W Wolf’s Frenzy first, then keep attacking the target marked with Kindred E Mounting Dread using Kindred Q Dance of Arrows and basic attacks. Use the attack speed from Kindred Q Dance of Arrows to build toward Kindred E Mounting Dread’s pounce, but don’t switch targets along the way.
Poppy.escape: Right after you make Poppy use Poppy E Heroic Charge is your chance to engage. Confirm that Poppy W Steadfast Presence has ended, then close in with Kindred Q Dance of Arrows. If Poppy E Heroic Charge is still available, restrict her movement with the slow from Kindred E Mounting Dread.
Poppy.fight: Fight after Poppy W Steadfast Presence ends or Poppy E Heroic Charge is down. Place Kindred W Wolf’s Frenzy first, then position and attack inside the zone with Kindred Q Dance of Arrows. Poppy’s armor increases as her health gets low, so check your finishing damage before chasing.
Poppy.phase: Early on, Kindred is fragile and slow, so prioritize farming and marks over forced fights. Look to duel from midgame once marks and attack speed items have built up. As marks increase your range later, keep your distance while fighting the melee Poppy.
Poppy.watch: Don’t dash in with Kindred Q Dance of Arrows while Poppy W Steadfast Presence is active. Stand in open space, since Poppy E Heroic Charge can stun you against a wall. If you’re hit by the first strike of Poppy Q Hammer Shock, walk out of the remaining zone. If Poppy charges Poppy R Keeper’s Verdict, move sideways out of its path.

Rengar.laning: Early on, farm your camps and collect Kindred P Mark of the Kindred instead of forcing an encounter with Rengar. Plan your route around the mark, but only go for marks deep in the enemy jungle without vision when your team has lane priority. If Rengar is out of sight, avoid brush edges and secure vision in brush.
Rengar.teamfight: After an ally starts the fight, place Kindred W Wolf's Frenzy behind your team and attack while repositioning with Kindred Q Dance of Arrows from within it. Watch out for Rengar R Thrill of the Hunt; don't move ahead of your frontline and stay within vision. If Rengar dives onto an allied carry, save them with Kindred R Lamb's Respite and lower the enemy's health so you can finish them when the zone ends.
Rengar.build: Get Grievous Wounds to counter healing from Rengar W Battle Roar, and consider Mortal Reminder to match a basic-attack-focused damage pattern. Build armor first because Rengar's main damage is physical. However, armor cannot block the magic damage from Rengar W Battle Roar.
Rengar.combo: Wait until Rengar W Battle Roar is down, then place Kindred W Wolf's Frenzy first. Follow with Kindred E Mounting Dread to slow and mark him, then use Kindred Q Dance of Arrows for attack speed and repeatedly basic attack the same target. Reposition with Kindred Q Dance of Arrows within Kindred W Wolf's Frenzy.
Rengar.escape: The opportunity to fight comes after you dodge Rengar E Bola Strike and he has already leapt in from brush. Rengar has no skill that lets him create distance on his own, so attack while adjusting your spacing with Kindred Q Dance of Arrows. If Rengar's resource bar is full, watch for an empowered ability and don't start a trade.
Rengar.fight: Trade damage after Rengar's resource bar is empty and Rengar W Battle Roar is down. If you dodge Rengar E Bola Strike, use Kindred Q Dance of Arrows to position, then apply the slow from Kindred E Mounting Dread and keep attacking the same target.
Rengar.phase: Early on, Kindred is fragile and has low movement speed, so prioritize marks and farming over forcing an encounter with Rengar. You can duel from mid game as you build marks and attack speed items. As your basic attack range increases from marks, you'll be better equipped to face the melee Rengar, but that growth is hard to count on if you miss marks.
Rengar.watch: Rengar P Unseen Predator lets him leap from brush and build up his resource, so avoid paths beside brush when he is out of sight. Rengar E Bola Strike roots when his resource bar is full, so dodge the throw before moving with Kindred Q Dance of Arrows. When Rengar R Thrill of the Hunt is active, don't roam alone at low health.

Taliyah.laning: Check the mark location first and plan your camp route in that direction. Only contest a mark deep in the enemy jungle without vision when your team has lane priority. Gank when an ally has reliable crowd control or Taliyah has pushed too far. If Taliyah disappears from the jungle, watch for her to use Taliyah P Rock Surfing and Taliyah R Weaver’s Wall to pressure another lane.
Taliyah.teamfight: After your team starts a fight, place Kindred W Wolf’s Frenzy behind your allies and attack from within it, adjusting your position with Kindred Q Dance of Arrows. Don’t stand in front while Taliyah E Unraveled Earth or Taliyah R Weaver’s Wall is available. If an enemy dives your team’s main damage dealer, save them with Kindred R Lamb’s Respite, but be ready to finish enemies as soon as it ends since they also survive and heal in the zone.
Taliyah.build: Most of the damage from Taliyah Q Threaded Volley and Taliyah E Unraveled Earth is magic damage, so build magic resistance first. Then, as Kindred stacks marks and prepares for midgame duels, get attack speed items.
Taliyah.combo: Place Kindred W Wolf’s Frenzy where Taliyah will stand, then mark her with Kindred E Mounting Dread. Weave in Kindred Q Dance of Arrows to gain attack speed, then keep basic attacking the same target to trigger the wolf’s pounce. If Taliyah E Unraveled Earth is active, start the combo from an angle that doesn’t cross the rock field with Kindred Q Dance of Arrows.
Taliyah.escape: Wait until both Taliyah E Unraveled Earth and Taliyah R Weaver’s Wall have been used before engaging, especially before Taliyah R Weaver’s Wall comes back up. Even if Taliyah E Unraveled Earth is down, avoid positions where Taliyah W Seismic Shove can push you toward the rock field. Use that opening to close the gap with Kindred Q Dance of Arrows and Kindred W Wolf’s Frenzy.
Taliyah.fight: While Taliyah E Unraveled Earth is active, go around the rock field instead of crossing it with Kindred Q Dance of Arrows. Once you’re on top of her, slow her with Kindred E Mounting Dread and keep attacking the same target. If you maintain damage, you can also stop her from escaping with Taliyah R Weaver’s Wall.
Taliyah.phase: Kindred is fragile and slow early, so prioritize farming and collecting marks over risky fights. Once you have marks and attack speed items in the midgame, you can start taking duels. Kindred’s increased range later also depends on stacking marks, so make sure you secure marks early.
Taliyah.watch: Taliyah Q Threaded Volley cannot change direction while being cast, so dodge it sideways with Kindred Q Dance of Arrows. Don’t use Kindred Q Dance of Arrows to dash across Taliyah’s rock field.

Vi.watch: Vi Q Vault Breaker deals more damage when charged, so move back or to the side when you see her wind up. Vi W Denting Blows shreds armor as she keeps hitting the same target, so don’t stay in a prolonged fight. Vi R Cease and Desist chases its target to the end and knocks them up, so don’t try to dodge it with Flash; stay near your allies.
Vi.laning: Early on, prioritize farming by routing toward marks. Only contest a mark deep in Vi’s jungle without vision when your team has lane priority. Gank when an ally has reliable crowd control or the enemy has pushed too far.
Vi.teamfight: Don’t step forward first while Vi Q Vault Breaker and Vi R Cease and Desist are available. After your team starts a fight, place Kindred W Wolf’s Frenzy behind your allies and attack from within it, adjusting your position with Kindred Q Dance of Arrows. If Vi’s engage catches your team’s main damage dealer, save them with Kindred R Lamb’s Respite, then finish enemies as soon as the zone ends.
Vi.build: Build armor first against Vi’s main damage. Vi W Denting Blows deals damage based on maximum health, so avoid relying only on health and consider an option that reduces Vi’s attack speed.
Vi.combo: When Vi Q Vault Breaker is down, place Kindred W Wolf’s Frenzy on Vi first. Apply Kindred E Mounting Dread, weave in Kindred Q Dance of Arrows, and keep basic attacking the same target. Don’t switch targets until Kindred E Mounting Dread’s pounce triggers.
Vi.escape: The moment after you force Vi Q Vault Breaker is an opportunity to close the gap with Kindred Q Dance of Arrows. If Vi is engaging with Vi R Cease and Desist, don’t force that opening; wait until she lands and the knock-up ends before moving.
Vi.fight: Fight after dodging or forcing Vi Q Vault Breaker. Attack from within Kindred W Wolf’s Frenzy, using Kindred Q Dance of Arrows to adjust your distance, and finish the trade before Vi W Denting Blows stacks up.
Vi.phase: Kindred is fragile early, so prioritize marks and farming over risky head-on fights with Vi. Look for duels from midgame onward, once you have marks and attack speed items. After your range increases, keep your distance while fighting the melee Vi.

XinZhao.teamfight: Don’t engage first. After your team starts a fight, place Kindred W Wolf’s Frenzy behind your allies and use Kindred Q Dance of Arrows to adjust your position. If Xin Zhao E Audacious Charge catches your team’s main damage dealer, you can save them with Kindred R Lamb’s Respite, but remember Xin Zhao will also survive inside the zone. Keep some space from your allies so Xin Zhao R Crescent Guard’s knockback doesn’t split your formation.
XinZhao.laning: Early on, don’t recklessly chase marks in the enemy jungle without vision; route your camps toward the marked side instead. Prioritize farming if you’re at high risk of running into Xin Zhao, and contest marks in the enemy jungle when your team has lane priority.
XinZhao.build: Build armor first against Xin Zhao’s main damage. If the healing from Xin Zhao P Determination is a problem, get healing reduction and armor penetration with Mortal Reminder.
XinZhao.combo: Place Kindred W Wolf’s Frenzy where the fight will happen. Apply Kindred E Mounting Dread to Xin Zhao, then keep attacking the same target with Kindred Q Dance of Arrows and basic attacks. When the third hit of Xin Zhao Q Three Talon Strike is coming, use Kindred Q Dance of Arrows to get out of range.
XinZhao.escape: The moment after you force Xin Zhao E Audacious Charge is an opportunity to fight while managing your distance with Kindred Q Dance of Arrows. If you’ve also dodged the third hit of Xin Zhao Q Three Talon Strike, you can keep attacking without risking a knock-up.
XinZhao.fight: Dodge the thrust from Xin Zhao W Wind Becomes Lightning to the side, then manage your distance after he uses Xin Zhao E Audacious Charge. When Xin Zhao R Crescent Guard is active, don’t force ranged attacks; counterattack once the immunity ends.
XinZhao.watch: Dodge the follow-up thrust of Xin Zhao W Wind Becomes Lightning by moving sideways. If you’ve been hit twice by the empowered basic attacks from Xin Zhao Q Three Talon Strike, use Kindred Q Dance of Arrows to get out of range before the third hit knocks you up. While Xin Zhao R Crescent Guard is active, don’t keep attacking from outside his spear range; wait for the immunity to end.
XinZhao.phase: In the early game, Kindred should prioritize marks and farming over forcing fights with Xin Zhao. Look for duels from the mid game, once marks and attack speed items have started to stack, and keep your distance when fighting Xin Zhao after your range increases. In late-game team fights, use the moment Xin Zhao R Crescent Guard ends as an opportunity to counterattack.

Briar.laning: Plan your camp route toward the mark, but only contest a deep mark in Briar’s jungle without vision when your allies have lane priority. Gank when an ally has reliable crowd control or the opponent has pushed the lane too far; otherwise, farm and look for marks through counterjungling. Don’t stay long in areas without vision, so you’re ready for Briar’s ganks.
Briar.teamfight: Kindred should not engage first. After an ally starts the fight, cast W Wolf’s Frenzy behind your team and attack while repositioning with Q Dance of Arrows. Stay behind your frontline so you aren’t the nearest target for Briar W Blood Frenzy / Snack Attack. If Briar engages on an allied key damage dealer, save them with Kindred R Lamb’s Respite, then finish the enemy as the zone ends.
Briar.watch: Briar Q Head Rush dashes in, stuns, and reduces armor, so use Kindred Q Dance of Arrows to create distance before it connects. When Briar E Chilling Scream starts charging, don’t stand with your back to a wall; get out of its area. If hit by Briar R Certain Death, move toward your allies and fight back together instead of trying to flee alone.
Briar.build: Build armor first because Briar’s main damage is physical. If Briar P Crimson Curse, W Blood Frenzy / Snack Attack, and E Chilling Scream healing make the duel drag on, get Mortal Reminder for Grievous Wounds.
Briar.combo: When Briar gets on you, cast Kindred W Wolf’s Frenzy first, then use E Mounting Dread to slow and mark her. Find a position where you can dodge Briar’s dash, and use Q Dance of Arrows inside the Wolf’s Frenzy zone.
Briar.escape: Don’t engage just because Briar Q Head Rush is down. Briar can close in again with W Blood Frenzy / Snack Attack and R Certain Death, so wait until her mobility and crowd control are down. Especially before Briar R Certain Death is back up, fight while controlling the distance with Kindred Q Dance of Arrows and W Wolf’s Frenzy.
Briar.fight: Early on, prioritize marks and farming instead of fighting Briar recklessly. When you fight, reposition with Q Dance of Arrows inside Kindred W Wolf’s Frenzy and keep attacking the same target. While Briar is in W Blood Frenzy / Snack Attack, she chases the nearest enemy, so keep your distance and fight back.
Briar.phase: Early on, Kindred is fragile and slow, while Briar is strong in early fights, so focus on marks and farming instead of fighting. Kindred can duel once marks and attack speed items build up in midgame. In late game, use the range gained from marks to keep your distance from nearby Briar, but if you missed marks, it will be harder to gain that advantage.

Elise.laning: Get vision to avoid giving up kills to Elise’s early ganks, and don’t push your lane too far when she’s missing. Kindred should plan camp routes toward the mark, but only contest a deep mark in the enemy jungle without vision when your allies have lane priority. Look for ganks when an ally has reliable crowd control or the opponent has pushed the lane too far.
Elise.teamfight: Kindred should not engage first. After an ally starts the fight, cast Kindred W Wolf’s Frenzy behind your team. Inside the zone, use Kindred Q Dance of Arrows to position against Elise’s engage and Elise E Cocoon while basic attacking. If an allied key damage dealer is caught, save them with Kindred R Lamb’s Respite and lower the enemy’s health in the meantime so you can finish them as the zone ends.
Elise.build: Build magic resistance first against the damage from Elise’s main abilities. Also consider armor because she deals basic attack damage. If healing from Elise P Spider Queen is a problem, get Mortal Reminder for Grievous Wounds.
Elise.combo: Cast Kindred W Wolf’s Frenzy first where you plan to fight. Apply Kindred E Mounting Dread to Elise, weave in Kindred Q Dance of Arrows to gain attack speed, then keep basic attacking the same target to trigger Wolf’s pounce. If Elise is airborne with E Rappel, wait for her to land before continuing your attacks.
Elise.escape: Just after Elise uses Q Neurotoxin / Venomous Bite is your chance to close in with Kindred Q Dance of Arrows. In particular, if you confirm both Elise E Cocoon and E Rappel are down, cast Kindred W Wolf’s Frenzy and turn the fight around.
Elise.fight: Early on, prioritize marks and farming instead of forcing a fight. Just after Elise uses Q Neurotoxin / Venomous Bite, look for a chance to attack while controlling the distance with Kindred Q Dance of Arrows. If Elise E Cocoon and E Rappel are also down, keep dealing damage while repositioning inside Kindred W Wolf’s Frenzy.
Elise.phase: Elise is threatening early because she looks for an advantage through ganks, so Kindred should avoid giving up kills and focus on marks and farming. Kindred can duel in midgame once marks and attack speed items are in place. After you collect enough marks to increase your basic attack range, fights become more favorable, but missing marks also delays that growth.
Elise.watch: Keep a minion or jungle monster between you and Elise, and reposition with Kindred Q Dance of Arrows when Cocoon flies toward you. Once health has dropped, if Elise transforms with Elise R Spider Form, she can look to finish the fight, so be ready to use Kindred R Lamb’s Respite.

Graves.laning: Early on, plan your camp route toward marks and prioritize farming and securing them. Attempt a deep mark in enemy territory without vision only when your team has lane priority. Look for ganks when an ally has reliable crowd control or the enemy has pushed too far; otherwise, clear vision and apply pressure with counter-jungling.
Graves.fight: Fight back or create distance while Graves reloads after firing two shots. In open terrain, put an ally or another unit between you and Graves to block his basic attacks, and attack while repositioning with Kindred Q Dance of Arrows inside Kindred W Wolf's Frenzy. Even if Graves E Quickdraw is down, do not chase recklessly if Graves R Collateral Damage is still available.
Graves.teamfight: Do not engage first. Wait for an ally to start the fight, then place Kindred W Wolf's Frenzy behind your team and attack while repositioning with Kindred Q Dance of Arrows. Keep an ally or another unit between you and Graves to block his basic attacks, and leave the area immediately if Graves W Smoke Screen traps you. Use Kindred R Lamb's Respite to save an allied carry who is caught or when an enemy moves in to contest an objective with Smite; account for enemies healing too, and finish them as the zone ends.
Graves.build: Get Plated Steelcaps early and prioritize armor against the main damage from Graves P New Destiny, Graves Q End of the Line, and Graves R Collateral Damage. Armor does not reduce the magic damage from Graves W Smoke Screen, so leave the smoke quickly.
Graves.combo: Place Kindred W Wolf's Frenzy where you plan to fight and battle inside its area. Apply Kindred E Mounting Dread to Graves, then use Kindred Q Dance of Arrows to increase your attack speed and keep basic attacking the same target to trigger Wolf's pounce. If Graves looks ready to escape with a mobility ability, apply Kindred E Mounting Dread's slow first, then position carefully so that leaving Kindred W Wolf's Frenzy does not interrupt Kindred Q Dance of Arrows' quick cooldown cycle.
Graves.escape: Leave Graves W Smoke Screen and regain vision before engaging. The chance to chase comes when both Graves E Quickdraw and Graves R Collateral Damage are down, or especially before Graves R Collateral Damage comes back. Place Kindred W Wolf's Frenzy and close the distance with Kindred Q Dance of Arrows.
Graves.phase: Early on, Kindred is fragile and slow, so farming and securing marks matter more than forcing fights with Graves. Start looking to duel in mid game once marks and attack speed items are in place, but pressure Graves through your pathing and vision so he has no time to build his growth stacks. Graves gets stronger as the game goes on, making the matchup harder, so do not miss early marks and slow his growth.
Graves.watch: Graves Q End of the Line detonates immediately when it hits a wall, so avoid fighting with your back to a wall or in narrow jungle passages. If Graves W Smoke Screen traps you, it blocks your vision and slows you; get out by the shortest route, then fight again. Graves E Quickdraw and Graves R Collateral Damage can both create distance, so do not chase deep just because one is down.

Rammus.laning: Early on, plan your camp route around the mark location and prioritize farming. Only go for marks in the enemy jungle without vision when your team has lane priority. If there are minions along Rammus Q Powerball's path, stand behind them to block his approach.
Rammus.teamfight: Don't engage first. After an ally starts the fight, place Kindred W Wolf's Frenzy behind your team. Stay out of the engage range of Rammus Q Powerball and R Soaring Slam, and use Kindred Q Dance of Arrows to reposition within the zone. If an allied carry is caught, save them with Kindred R Lamb's Respite, but account for enemies also surviving inside the zone and recovering when it ends, then finish them immediately after.
Rammus.build: Build magic resistance first against Rammus's main damage from Q Powerball, W Defensive Ball Curl, and R Soaring Slam. If you have to fight Rammus directly, consider percentage penetration over flat penetration against the increased resistances from W Defensive Ball Curl.
Rammus.combo: Place Kindred W Wolf's Frenzy where the opponent will stand. When Rammus W Defensive Ball Curl ends, apply Kindred E Mounting Dread, then use Kindred Q Dance of Arrows for attack speed and keep basic attacking the same target. If Rammus activates W Defensive Ball Curl, stop basic attacking and wait for its duration to end.
Rammus.escape: The window while Rammus R Soaring Slam is down is your chance to engage. If Rammus E Frenzying Taunt is also down, close the gap with Kindred Q Dance of Arrows and W Wolf's Frenzy.
Rammus.fight: Focus your damage after Rammus W Defensive Ball Curl ends. Place Kindred W Wolf's Frenzy outside the range of Rammus E Frenzying Taunt, then attack from within the zone while adjusting your spacing with Kindred Q Dance of Arrows. If Rammus looks ready to escape with Rammus R Soaring Slam, apply the slow from Kindred E Mounting Dread first.
Rammus.phase: Early on, Kindred is fragile and has low movement speed, so don't force fights with Rammus; collect marks and farm. Look to duel from mid game once you have marks and attack speed items, but stop attacking while Rammus W Defensive Ball Curl is active. In the late game, use the range gained from marks, and don't rely on that growth if you missed marks.
Rammus.watch: When you see Rammus Q Powerball, put minions between you and him, and stay outside the range of the Rammus E Frenzying Taunt that follows. When Rammus R Soaring Slam rolls in at top speed, dodge well clear of its area and move away from the landing spot. Stop basic attacking while Rammus W Defensive Ball Curl is active to avoid reflected damage.

Viego.laning: Early on, keep your camp route pointed toward the marked side, and only contest a mark deep in the enemy jungle without vision when your team has lane priority. Avoid paths covered by Viego E Harrowed Path, and don’t force a gank if your allies have no reliable crowd control or the enemy has not pushed too far. Back off from skirmishes you can’t win without giving up a kill.
Viego.teamfight: After your team starts a fight, place Kindred W Wolf’s Frenzy behind your allies and use Kindred Q Dance of Arrows to adjust your position while basic attacking from within it. Don’t stand forward while Viego W Spectral Maw and Viego R Heartbreaker are available. If an enemy catches your team’s main damage dealer, prevent the kill with Kindred R Lamb’s Respite. The zone also keeps Viego alive, so lower his health before it ends and finish him immediately afterward. Keep your distance from the spot where an ally dies and watch for possession from Viego P Sovereign’s Domination.
Viego.build: Build armor first against the physical damage from Viego Q Blade of the Ruined King and Viego R Heartbreaker. If the duel drags on, get healing reduction with Mortal Reminder to reduce healing from Viego P Sovereign’s Domination and Viego Q Blade of the Ruined King. Viego Q Blade of the Ruined King deals extra damage based on current health, so avoid stacking a lot of health alone.
Viego.combo: Place Kindred W Wolf’s Frenzy where the enemy will fight. Slow the target with Kindred E Mounting Dread, use Kindred Q Dance of Arrows to gain attack speed, then keep basic attacking the same target to trigger the wolf’s pounce. If Viego might escape with Viego W Spectral Maw or Viego R Heartbreaker, apply Kindred E Mounting Dread early.
Viego.escape: If only Viego W Spectral Maw is down, don’t rush in because he can escape with Viego R Heartbreaker. If both abilities are down, or before Viego R Heartbreaker comes back up, close the gap with Kindred Q Dance of Arrows and Kindred W Wolf’s Frenzy and fight. If Viego W Spectral Maw is charging, dodge sideways first to avoid the stun.
Viego.fight: Early on, prioritize marks and farming over forcing a fight with Viego. When fighting, place Kindred W Wolf’s Frenzy first and use Kindred Q Dance of Arrows to manage your distance while attacking from within the zone. Look to engage after both Viego W Spectral Maw and Viego R Heartbreaker are down.
Viego.phase: Kindred is fragile and slow early, so marks and farming matter more than risky fights with Viego. Look for duels from midgame onward as you collect marks and attack speed items. Once your range increases, keep your distance while fighting melee champion Viego. Focus on getting marks early, since missing them makes it hard to gain the range advantage later.
Viego.watch: Viego W Spectral Maw stuns for longer the more it is charged, so dodge sideways with Kindred Q Dance of Arrows when you see him charging. When Viego E Harrowed Path covers terrain, watch for Viego camouflaged within it and go around the path. When your health is low, don’t step forward recklessly because you’re an easy target for Viego R Heartbreaker.

Zac.laning: Early on, prioritize Kindred P Mark of the Kindred and farming over recklessly running into Zac. Route camps toward the marked side, but only contest a mark deep in Zac’s jungle without vision when your team has lane priority. Look for ganks when an ally has reliable crowd control or the enemy has pushed too far.
Zac.teamfight: Don’t stand forward while Zac E Elastic Slingshot is available. After your team starts a fight, place Kindred W Wolf’s Frenzy behind your allies. Once you’ve absorbed Zac’s engage, use Kindred Q Dance of Arrows to create distance and basic attack from within the zone to avoid Zac W Unstable Matter’s damage. If Zac’s engage catches your team’s main damage dealer, save them with Kindred R Lamb’s Respite and be ready to finish Zac as the zone ends.
Zac.build: Get healing reduction against the healing from Zac P Cell Division, and choose Mortal Reminder to complement Kindred’s sustained basic attack damage. Build magic resistance against the damage from Zac Q Stretching Strikes, Zac W Unstable Matter, and Zac E Elastic Slingshot. Zac W Unstable Matter deals damage based on maximum health, so avoid stacking a lot of health alone.
Zac.combo: Place Kindred W Wolf’s Frenzy first, then slow Zac with Kindred E Mounting Dread. Follow with Kindred Q Dance of Arrows to gain attack speed, then keep basic attacking the same target to trigger Kindred E Mounting Dread’s finishing damage. During the fight, use Kindred Q Dance of Arrows to reposition within Kindred W Wolf’s Frenzy.
Zac.escape: The moment after Zac E Elastic Slingshot is down is your chance to engage. Avoid the landing spot, then close the gap with Kindred Q Dance of Arrows and Kindred W Wolf’s Frenzy, and keep Zac from escaping with Kindred E Mounting Dread’s slow.
Zac.fight: Fight while managing your distance right after you dodge or force Zac E Elastic Slingshot. Place Kindred W Wolf’s Frenzy where Zac will fight, then keep basic attacking while using Kindred Q Dance of Arrows to reposition from within the zone. Step on the blobs Zac drops to stop him from healing.
Zac.phase: Kindred is fragile and slow early, so prioritize marks and farming over risky fights with Zac. Duels become viable from midgame onward as you collect marks and attack speed items. Once your range increases, you can keep your distance against melee champions like Zac. Even in the late game, you can’t count on this growth if you failed to collect marks in time.
Zac.watch: Zac E Elastic Slingshot is a charged knock-up engage, so avoid its landing spot if you see him charging behind a wall. Once he gets close, create distance while watching out for the slow and knock-up from Zac Q Stretching Strikes and the maximum-health-based damage from Zac W Unstable Matter. Step on the blobs Zac drops as you move past them to prevent him from healing.

Amumu.teamfight: Don’t group with allies or engage first while Amumu R Curse of the Sad Mummy is available. After an ally starts the fight, cast Kindred W Wolf’s Frenzy behind your team and attack while repositioning with Kindred Q Dance of Arrows inside the zone. If a key ally is about to die after Amumu engages, save them with Kindred R Lamb’s Respite, then finish the enemy as the zone ends.
Amumu.laning: Early on, plan your camp route around the mark, but only contest a deep mark in Amumu’s jungle without vision when your allies have lane priority.
Amumu.watch: If Amumu Q Bandage Toss hits you, it stuns you and lets him close in, and Amumu R Curse of the Sad Mummy can then lock down your allies too. Stand with a jungle monster between you and him or dodge the bandage with Kindred Q Dance of Arrows. Don’t group with your allies while Amumu has his ultimate.
Amumu.build: If Amumu Q Bandage Toss and Amumu R Curse of the Sad Mummy lock you down and get you killed, prioritize a cleanse or tenacity. Build magic resistance against Amumu’s magic damage. If Amumu E Tantrum’s physical damage reduction is blocking your damage, consider armor penetration.
Amumu.combo: Cast Kindred W Wolf’s Frenzy first, then apply Kindred E Mounting Dread to Amumu. Use Kindred Q Dance of Arrows and basic attacks inside the zone, continuing to attack the same target to trigger Wolf’s pounce.
Amumu.escape: Go in while Amumu Q Bandage Toss and Amumu R Curse of the Sad Mummy are down. Amumu has no ability to create distance on his own, so use Kindred Q Dance of Arrows to close in and chase him inside Kindred W Wolf’s Frenzy.
Amumu.fight: Engage after dodging Amumu Q Bandage Toss or once Amumu R Curse of the Sad Mummy is down. Use Kindred Q Dance of Arrows to adjust your distance inside Kindred W Wolf’s Frenzy, and don’t stay near Amumu for long while taking damage from Amumu W Despair.
Amumu.phase: Look for duels from midgame onward, once you have marks and attack speed items. After your range increases, attack while keeping your distance from Amumu. Missing marks weakens this growth curve.

JarvanIV.laning: Route your camps toward marks, but attempt a mark in enemy territory without vision only when your team has lane priority.
JarvanIV.teamfight: Do not engage first. Place Kindred W Wolf's Frenzy behind your team, then attack while repositioning with Kindred Q Dance of Arrows inside its area.
JarvanIV.build: After that, get the attack speed items Kindred needs to duel in mid game.
JarvanIV.combo: Place Kindred W Wolf's Frenzy where you plan to fight.

Kayn.laning: Route your camps toward marks, but attempt a deep mark in Kayn's territory without vision only when your team has lane priority. If you see the wall-edge warning that signals Kayn E Shadow Step, stop trading damage and retreat toward your turret. Look for ganks when an ally has reliable crowd control or the enemy has pushed too far.
Kayn.teamfight: Do not engage first. Wait for an ally to start the fight, then place Kindred W Wolf's Frenzy behind your team. Inside its area, use Kindred Q Dance of Arrows to dodge Kayn Q Reaping Slash and W Blade's Reach while basic attacking. If an allied carry is caught by Kayn's engage, save them with Kindred R Lamb's Respite, then finish enemies as the zone ends.
Kayn.build: Prioritize armor against the physical damage from Kayn Q Reaping Slash, Kayn W Blade's Reach, and Kayn R Umbral Trespass. If Kayn transforms into a Rhaast who keeps healing, get healing reduction later with Mortal Reminder.
Kayn.combo: Place Kindred W Wolf's Frenzy at the fight location first. If Kayn looks ready to escape with Q Reaping Slash or R Umbral Trespass, apply Kindred E Mounting Dread early to slow him. Then use Kindred Q Dance of Arrows to increase your attack speed and keep basic attacking the same target to trigger E's pounce.
Kayn.escape: Do not engage hastily when only Kayn Q Reaping Slash is down, since Kayn can escape with Kayn R Umbral Trespass. Dodge Kayn W Blade's Reach, then close the gap with Kindred Q Dance of Arrows and W Wolf's Frenzy while Kayn R Umbral Trespass is down.
Kayn.fight: Early on, prioritize marks and farming over forcing solo fights. Look for a fight after dodging Kayn W Blade's Reach and before Kayn R Umbral Trespass comes back. Place Kindred W Wolf's Frenzy first, then position with Q Dance of Arrows and basic attack inside its area.
Kayn.phase: Kayn is weak before transforming, but Kindred is fragile early too, so avoid forced duels and grow through marks and farming. Kindred can duel in mid game once marks and attack speed items have accumulated. After marks increase your range, you can keep your distance while fighting nearby Kayn, but missing marks weakens this growth pattern.
Kayn.watch: Dodge the straight-line hit from Kayn W Blade's Reach with Kindred Q Dance of Arrows. If Kayn W hits you, he can follow with Kayn R Umbral Trespass, so adjust your distance as Kayn casts W. Be careful about fighting at close range because Kayn Q Reaping Slash deals damage based on your maximum health.

Lillia.laning: Plan your camp route toward the mark, and only go for marks deep in the enemy jungle without vision when your team has lane priority. If you don’t know where Lillia is, don’t blindly pass through narrow jungle entrances or river paths where it’s hard to dodge Lillia E Swirlseed. Gank when an ally has reliable crowd control or the enemy has pushed their lane too far; otherwise, prioritize farming and marks.
Lillia.phase: Early on, Kindred is fragile and slow, so avoid forced fights with the enemy jungler and prioritize marks and farming. You can duel effectively from midgame once marks and attack speed items are in place, so fight when you’ve dodged Lillia’s abilities and Lillia W Watch Out! Eep! is down. Late game, use the extra range from marks, but if you’ve missed marks, take a safe position instead of relying on that growth.
Lillia.teamfight: Don’t engage first. After an ally starts the fight, place Kindred W Wolf’s Frenzy behind your team and attack while repositioning inside it with Kindred Q Dance of Arrows. Save your allies’ immobilizing crowd control to catch Lillia when she comes in from the side, and dodge the center of Lillia W Watch Out! Eep! by moving sideways. If an allied carry is caught, protect them with Kindred R Lamb’s Respite, but remember that enemies also survive and heal when it ends; finish them right after the zone expires.
Lillia.build: Build magic resistance first against Lillia’s main damage. Lillia P Dream-Laden Bough deals damage based on your maximum health, so be careful about investing heavily in health alone. If the healing from Lillia P Dream-Laden Bough is a problem, get Mortal Reminder for Grievous Wounds and armor penetration.
Lillia.combo: After Lillia W Watch Out! Eep! is down, place Kindred W Wolf’s Frenzy where she will stand. Slow her with Kindred E Mounting Dread, build attack speed with Kindred Q Dance of Arrows, then keep basic attacking the same target to trigger Wolf’s pounce. Leaving the zone interrupts Kindred Q Dance of Arrows’ quick cooldown, so reposition as you fight.
Lillia.escape: Right after you make Lillia use Lillia W Watch Out! Eep! is your chance to close the gap. Dodge Lillia Q Blooming Blows and Lillia E Swirlseed to deny her movement speed stacks and the condition for Lillia R Lilting Lullaby, then go in with Kindred Q Dance of Arrows. If she looks ready to escape with Watch Out! Eep!, apply the slow from Kindred E Mounting Dread first.
Lillia.fight: Don’t chase while Lillia is building movement speed by landing abilities. Dodge her abilities, then close in with Kindred Q Dance of Arrows when she has no stacks, especially right after she uses Lillia W Watch Out! Eep! Keep attacking the same target while repositioning inside Kindred W Wolf’s Frenzy with Kindred Q Dance of Arrows.
Lillia.watch: Being hit by Lillia Q Blooming Blows or Lillia E Swirlseed enables Lillia R Lilting Lullaby to put you to sleep, so dodge them even when your health is high. If Lillia R Lilting Lullaby affects you, move to safety while you can still act before falling asleep. When you see the cast animation for Lillia W Watch Out! Eep!, move sideways to avoid the center hit.

Nidalee.laning: Plan your camp route toward Kindred P Mark of the Kindred and keep farming. Only go for marks deep in the enemy jungle without vision when your team has lane priority. Check for traps at entrances, and avoid forced ganks unless an ally has reliable crowd control or the enemy has overextended.
Nidalee.phase: Early on, Kindred is fragile and loses to the enemy jungler for a long stretch, so prioritize marks and farming. Look to duel from midgame, once marks and attack speed items have built up. To make use of the extra range from marks later, don’t miss early marks.
Nidalee.teamfight: Don’t engage first. After an ally starts the fight, place Kindred W Wolf’s Frenzy behind your team. Attack while repositioning inside it with Kindred Q Dance of Arrows, and watch for Nidalee W Bushwhack / Pounce to engage. If an allied carry is caught, save them with Kindred R Lamb’s Respite, but remember that enemies also heal, and finish them right after the zone ends.
Nidalee.build: Nidalee’s main damage is magic damage, so prioritize magic resistance over armor. If the healing from Nidalee E Primal Surge / Swipe is a problem, get Mortal Reminder for Grievous Wounds and armor penetration.
Nidalee.combo: Once Nidalee W Bushwhack / Pounce is down, place Kindred W Wolf’s Frenzy first and apply a slow and mark with Kindred E Mounting Dread. Follow with Kindred Q Dance of Arrows to build attack speed, then keep basic attacking without switching targets to trigger pounce.
Nidalee.escape: Right after Nidalee W Bushwhack / Pounce is used is your chance to engage. Nidalee has no crowd control, so if you dodge her spear and traps, close in with Kindred Q Dance of Arrows and attack.
Nidalee.fight: Start a fight after dodging Nidalee Q Javelin Toss and her traps. Right after Nidalee W Bushwhack / Pounce is used, close the gap with Kindred Q Dance of Arrows, then reposition and keep attacking the same target inside Kindred W Wolf’s Frenzy.
Nidalee.watch: Nidalee Q Javelin Toss deals more damage the farther away you are, so be especially careful to dodge it at long range. Watch for Nidalee W Bushwhack / Pounce traps at jungle entrances and in the river. If you’re hit by a spear or trap, prepare for Nidalee W Bushwhack / Pounce to close in and Nidalee Q Javelin Toss / Takedown to finish you.

Sejuani.laning: Check the mark location and plan your camp route in that direction, but only go for marks deep in Sejuani's jungle without vision when your team has lane priority. Gank when an ally has reliable crowd control or the enemy has pushed too far. If there's no opening, build marks through farming and counterjungling.
Sejuani.teamfight: Don't stand forward while Sejuani Q Arctic Assault is available. After an ally starts the fight, place Kindred W Wolf's Frenzy behind your team. Use basic attacks from within the zone while dodging Sejuani's engage with Kindred Q Dance of Arrows. If an allied carry is about to die after being caught, use Kindred R Lamb's Respite, but account for enemies also surviving and healing when the zone ends, then finish them immediately after.
Sejuani.build: Build magic resistance first against Sejuani's main damage, and consider tenacity if you are held by crowd control from Q, E, and R for too long. Sejuani P Fury of the North scales with max health, so be careful about investing heavily in health alone, and build attack speed items for mid-game duels.
Sejuani.combo: Place Kindred W Wolf's Frenzy first, then target Sejuani with Kindred E Mounting Dread while Sejuani Q Arctic Assault is down. Follow with Kindred Q Dance of Arrows for attack speed and repeatedly basic attack the same target to trigger E's pounce.
Sejuani.escape: The moment after you force Sejuani to use Q Arctic Assault is your window to close the gap while adjusting your position with Kindred Q Dance of Arrows. If Sejuani has already used E Permafrost's stun, there's a brief window before stacks can build again, but create distance to avoid her first basic attack right after the stun.
Sejuani.fight: The moment after Sejuani Q Arctic Assault is down is your chance to fight. Place Kindred W Wolf's Frenzy where you plan to fight, then keep attacking the same target while repositioning with Kindred Q Dance of Arrows inside the zone. If Sejuani P Fury of the North has activated slow immunity, deal damage first to give yourself time for her armor to wear off; then you can use the slow from Kindred E Mounting Dread.
Sejuani.phase: Early on, Sejuani has low kill pressure and damage, leaving room to contest jungle control, but Kindred is also fragile, so prioritize marks and farming over forcing a direct fight. Look to duel in mid game once you have marks and attack speed items, and in the late game, use the range gained from marks to attack Sejuani while keeping your distance.
Sejuani.watch: Sejuani Q Arctic Assault and Sejuani R Glacial Prison can lead into a stun, so dodge sideways when you see their windups. If you're hit by the first strike of Sejuani W Winter's Wrath, use Kindred Q Dance of Arrows to get out of range before its second strike. Sejuani and her melee allies can build stacks of Sejuani E Permafrost, so create distance as the stacks build.

Shyvana.laning: Early on, pressure Shyvana to stop her from building Shyvana P Scalemail stacks through camps and objectives, but don't force fights as fragile Kindred. Plan your camp route toward marks, and only go for marks deep in the enemy jungle without vision when your team has lane priority. Gank when an ally has reliable crowd control or the enemy has pushed too far.
Shyvana.teamfight: Don't engage first. After an ally starts the fight, place Kindred W Wolf's Frenzy behind your team and attack while repositioning with Kindred Q Dance of Arrows inside the zone. Right after an allied carry is caught by Shyvana's engage, Kindred R Lamb's Respite can save them, but keep in mind that Shyvana will also survive if she's inside the zone.
Shyvana.build: If you need to counter healing from Shyvana W Inferno Aegis, get Grievous Wounds from Mortal Reminder. Build magic resistance first against the magic damage from Shyvana W Inferno Aegis, E Molten Burst, and R Dragon's Descent, and also get armor against her basic attack damage.
Shyvana.combo: Place Kindred W Wolf's Frenzy where Shyvana will stand. Slow her with Kindred E Mounting Dread, then weave in Kindred Q Dance of Arrows to gain attack speed and repeatedly basic attack without switching targets to trigger Wolf's pounce. Adjust your spacing with Kindred Q Dance of Arrows inside Kindred W Wolf's Frenzy.
Shyvana.escape: Look for an opening when Shyvana R Dragon's Descent is down and her Fury meter is empty. Shyvana has no skill that lets her create distance on her own, so follow with Kindred Q Dance of Arrows and Kindred W Wolf's Frenzy, then slow her with Kindred E Mounting Dread.
Shyvana.fight: Pressure Shyvana when her Fury meter is empty, and use Kindred Q Dance of Arrows to reposition if she closes in with Shyvana R Dragon's Descent. After Shyvana lands, apply the slow from Kindred E Mounting Dread and keep attacking the same target. The moment she returns to human form after her transformation ends is also a chance to counterattack.
Shyvana.phase: Early on, Shyvana is weak without accumulated stacks, but Kindred is also fragile, so collect marks and farm while hindering Shyvana's camp and objective growth instead of forcing a fight. A duel becomes viable in mid game once Kindred has marks and attack speed items. Shyvana P Scalemail stacks accumulate permanently, making things harder as the game goes on, so early pressure and securing marks are important.
Shyvana.watch: Shyvana R Dragon's Descent is unstoppable as she charges, so don't try to stop her mid-flight with Kindred E Mounting Dread. Create distance from the landing spot and avoid the slow and max-health-based damage from Shyvana E Molten Burst. Shyvana Q Emberstrike is dangerous when she's close enough to basic attack, so don't give her that distance.

Udyr.laning: Plan your camp route toward the mark, and only go for marks deep in the enemy jungle without vision when your team has lane priority. Secure vision at key paths and jungle entrances so you can track Udyr's route, and avoid forcing an invade when he is out of sight. Look to gank when an ally has reliable crowd control or the enemy has pushed too far.
Udyr.teamfight: Don't engage first. After an ally starts the fight, place Kindred W Wolf's Frenzy behind your team and attack while repositioning with Kindred Q Dance of Arrows inside it. Don't stand forward while Udyr E Blazing Stampede is available, and target weaker enemies behind Udyr, who is toughened by defensive items and Udyr W Iron Mantle. If Udyr dives onto an allied carry, save them with Kindred R Lamb's Respite, and lower the enemy's health beforehand so you can finish them when the zone ends.
Udyr.build: Build armor first against Udyr's basic-attack-focused damage. However, Udyr Q Wilding Claw deals mixed damage and Udyr R Wingborne Storm deals magic damage, so armor alone won't block all of it. If healing from Udyr W Iron Mantle is a problem, get Mortal Reminder for both Grievous Wounds and armor penetration.
Udyr.combo: Place Kindred W Wolf's Frenzy where you plan to fight and stay within the zone. Slow Udyr with Kindred E Mounting Dread, then follow with Kindred Q Dance of Arrows and basic attacks to keep hitting the same target. Kindred E Mounting Dread's finishing damage scales with missing health, so meet that condition after Udyr has lost health.
Udyr.escape: The window to counterattack or escape comes after you've absorbed one stun from Udyr E Blazing Stampede or right after he uses it to engage. During the awakened state of Udyr E Blazing Stampede, immobilizing effects do not work, so adjust your distance with the slow from Kindred E Mounting Dread and Kindred Q Dance of Arrows after the awakening ends. Don't waste Q before Udyr approaches and lose your escape tool.
Udyr.fight: Lower Udyr's health with basic attacks before he gets close, but save Kindred Q Dance of Arrows to respond to Udyr E Blazing Stampede. When Udyr W Iron Mantle's shield wears off, use Q to reposition and focus your attacks from within Kindred W Wolf's Frenzy. The moment after Udyr E Blazing Stampede is down is also a chance to fight.
Udyr.phase: Early on, Kindred is fragile and has low movement speed, so prioritize marks and farming over forcing a direct fight with Udyr. You can duel from mid game as marks and attack speed items build up, and once your range increases, you can pressure the melee Udyr from outside his range. Missing marks weakens that growth, so plan your early route carefully for the late game as well.
Udyr.watch: Udyr E Blazing Stampede quickly closes the gap and stuns, so create distance right after he activates a stance and save Kindred Q Dance of Arrows to disengage. If Udyr gets close, you'll take max-health-based damage from Udyr Q Wilding Claw and empowered basic attacks; if the slow from Udyr R Wingborne Storm is added, it becomes harder to keep your distance.

Fiddlesticks.laning: Early on, route through camps toward the mark, but only contest a deep mark in the enemy jungle without vision when your allies have lane priority. If Fiddlesticks is missing, check vision in the bushes behind lanes and along his approach routes, and don’t enter narrow paths without vision.
Fiddlesticks.teamfight: After an ally starts the fight, cast Kindred W Wolf’s Frenzy behind your team and attack while repositioning with Kindred Q Dance of Arrows inside the zone. Spread out so multiple allies aren’t hit by Fiddlesticks R Crowstorm. If a key damage dealer is caught by the engage, save them with Kindred R Lamb’s Respite and lower the enemy’s health in advance so you can finish them as the zone ends.
Fiddlesticks.build: Get Grievous Wounds against healing from Fiddlesticks W Bountiful Harvest, and consider Mortal Reminder to fit Kindred’s sustained attack pattern. Build magic resistance rather than armor against Fiddlesticks’ damage.
Fiddlesticks.escape: Once Fiddlesticks Q Terrify and Fiddlesticks E Reap’s silence are down, it’s also a chance to close in with Kindred Q Dance of Arrows and fight.
Fiddlesticks.fight: When Fiddlesticks uses W Bountiful Harvest, don’t stand there and let him channel on you; reposition with Kindred Q Dance of Arrows to avoid the damage over time.
Fiddlesticks.phase: Kindred is fragile early on, so prioritize farming and securing marks over risky head-on fights. You can look for duels in midgame once marks and attack speed items are in place. In late game, use the range gained from your accumulated marks, but don’t stand in front while Fiddlesticks R Crowstorm is available.
Fiddlesticks.combo: First cast Kindred W Wolf's Frenzy, then slow the target with Kindred E Mounting Dread. Follow up with Kindred Q Dance of Arrows to increase your attack speed, then keep basic attacking the same target to trigger E’s pounce.
Fiddlesticks.watch: Fiddlesticks R Crowstorm enters after channeling, so move out of its range when you see it being cast. Abilities can apply fear when they hit you from out of sight, so watch for ambushes if Fiddlesticks hasn’t been seen in a brush for a while, and don’t pass by a Scarecrow Effigy without checking.

Hecarim.laning: Route your camps toward marks, but go for a mark in Hecarim's territory without vision only when your team has lane priority. Try to gank when an ally has reliable crowd control or the enemy has pushed too far.
Hecarim.teamfight: Do not engage first while Hecarim E Devastating Charge and Hecarim R Onslaught of Shadows are available, and spread out from your allies so several of you are not feared at once. Wait for an ally to start the fight, then place Kindred W Wolf's Frenzy behind your team and attack while repositioning with Kindred Q Dance of Arrows inside its area. If Hecarim dives onto a carry and they are about to die, save them with Kindred R Lamb's Respite, but account for Hecarim surviving inside the zone and healing when it ends.
Hecarim.combo: Place Kindred W Wolf's Frenzy where you plan to start the fight.
Hecarim.escape: Do not engage just because Hecarim E Devastating Charge is down. Fight by closing the gap with Kindred Q Dance of Arrows and Kindred W Wolf's Frenzy when Hecarim R Onslaught of Shadows is also down or before it comes back.
Hecarim.fight: Early on, do not force fights with Hecarim; prioritize marks and farming. When fighting, place Kindred W Wolf's Frenzy first and use Kindred Q Dance of Arrows to manage distance while basic attacking inside its area.
Hecarim.phase: Early on, Kindred is fragile and slow while Hecarim clears camps quickly, so secure marks and farm instead of fighting him directly. Look to duel from mid game, once marks and attack speed items have accumulated. After your range increases, keep your distance and attack melee champion Hecarim. If you miss marks, this growth pattern is hard to achieve, so your late-game plan depends on securing them.
Hecarim.build: Build armor first to mitigate the physical damage from Hecarim Q Rampage and Hecarim E Devastating Charge. If the healing from Hecarim W Spirit of Dread is a problem, get Mortal Reminder for Grievous Wounds and armor penetration.
Hecarim.watch: Hecarim E Devastating Charge deals more damage and knocks back farther the farther he has run, so break vision or move toward your allies when he starts building distance. Hecarim R Onslaught of Shadows charges in and applies fear, so avoid grouping up in team fights and be ready to dodge with Kindred Q Dance of Arrows.

Nunu.laning: Plan Kindred’s camp route toward marks, but only go for marks deep in the enemy jungle without vision when your team has lane priority. If an ally has no reliable crowd control and the enemy hasn’t overextended, choose farming and counterjungling over ganking.
